main_text.p: ut olim Hadrianus ad Rufum Proconsulem, quam ipsis testibus auditis & examinatis.

II. In prima ergo acie Graecos collocamus, qui communi suffragio Paulo adscripsere Epistolam. Justinus Philosophus qui & Martyr, celebratus sub Antonino Pio, A.C. cL. nusquam sane aperte Epistolam citat expresso Pauli nomine. At citat aliquoties eadem cum Paulinis aliis serie, ut ejusdem sane authoris, V.g. Libro Eἀpistolōn ... Ἀ[?]poriῖn ad Quaest. LXXI, tria citat loca conjunctim ex Paulo, tacito nomine Hebr. 1.2. ἐπτ ἐσχάτων τῶν ἡμερῶν τύτων ἐλάλησεν &c. 1.Cor. x.11. εἰς ἐν τῆ συντελεία τῶν αὶωνων κατήντησεν. Gal. iv.4. ὅτε δὲ ἦλθε τὸ πλήρωμα τοῦ χρόνου. Quod si ipse hic libor controversus sit multis atque irreptitius, alibi etiam a Justino ex eadem Epistola citantur, quanquam implicitè, nec nominato authore, sed quod Justino familiare.
III. Irenaeus, proximus aetati Apostolorum, Lugdunensis Episcopus, Polycarpi discipulus, Justino fere aequalis, certe huic citatus Libro illo Quaest. & Resp.

page.notes: Greek citations in the body are transcribed from a small, blurred scan; the Greek of 1 Cor. 10.11 and the title of the Libro reference (E...pistolōn / Ἀ...pori...) are doubtful and should be checked against the original. The first line of the Greek of Gal. 4.4 is also uncertain. Italic and roman distinctions in the names are read from the scan.
